entries.title: Persuasion Listening: Who Skips the Walk?
entries.hook: Three people walk to Winthrop, but one Elliot refuses. Who stays behind?

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: Mary Elliot would not join the walk to Winthrop. She declared she could not possibly walk there and back again.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: So Charles and Henrietta went, and Anne walked with them, while Mary kept safely at the cottage.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: Listen for the reason before the name: the refusal comes first, the person is confirmed after.

entries.prompt: Who refuses to go to Winthrop?
entries.visualBrief: Elegant Regency country lane with three adult figures walking toward a distant farmhouse and one adult woman visible at a cottage window, restrained morning light, hands fully out of frame, no readable text.

entries.title: Interview English: Catch the Final Question
entries.hook: An interviewer's final sentence is never small talk.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: We will call the successful candidate by Friday. Now, one last question: why do you want this role?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Because the role matches the reporting work I already do, and I want to do it with a larger team.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Good. Remember the promised call, and answer the last question with one reason only.

entries.visualBrief: Bright modern office interview scene, two adult professionals seated across a small table with a folder between them, chest-up framing, hands below frame, teal and warm grey palette, no readable text.

entries.title: Persuasion: The Return of Charles Hayter
entries.hook: Charles Hayter leaves the field. How does he return?

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: Charles Hayter felt slighted and seemed to quit the field after Captain Wentworth's arrival.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: But Charles and Henrietta returned to the cottage, bringing, as may be conjectured, Charles Hayter with them.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: The inclusion itself is the forgiveness. No grand speech is required.

entries.answer: He returns with them, accepted again.
entries.visualBrief: Warm Regency cottage doorway at dusk with two adult young people welcoming a third adult gentleman, soft amber light, restrained relief in posture, hands mostly out of frame, no readable text.

entries.title: Interview English: Name One Reason
entries.hook: One clean reason beats five nervous ones.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I want this role because I already do this reporting work, and I do it well.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: That is one clear reason. Candidates who list five reasons usually lose the thread.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: So I will keep one reason and one example. The final answer is the clean one.

entries.prompt: How many reasons should the answer include?
entries.visualBrief: Bright anime office corner with an adult woman reviewing interview notes beside a laptop, upper body only, hands below frame, cream blue and coral palette, no readable text.
